# FDGA023

> DO chop before the first argument or parameter, indent one indentation level, and include one argument or parameter per line when a method declaration or method invocation is exceedingly long.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section A.1.3 Indent Usage.

This is a coding style convention. The book treats the appendix A conventions as suggestions, so you can override it.

## How it is checked

- Check: fdg (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: FDGA023
- Automatic fix: yes
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Status: verified

Message: Place each argument or parameter of a long list on its own line, starting on the line after the opening parenthesis

A list is long when its line exceeds max_line_length (default 120). Scope: A parameter or argument list is treated as exceedingly long, because the author chose to wrap it, when a line break falls between its items (at a separator, or before the first item or any later item); it must then be chopped before the first item, indented one level, with one item per line. Line breaks only inside a single item (a lambda body, an initializer, a nested call or a continued expression) do not by themselves make the list wrapped, but a list whose line exceeds the length guide is still covered. A line that is long only because an enclosing conditional, ||, && or ?? expression joins short calls does not make their lists long; the list's own invocation, with the fluent chain it is part of, must exceed the guide (docs/noise-samples.md).

## From the book

```csharp
private void SomeMethod(
    int firstParameter,
    string secondParameter,
    bool thirdParameter,
    string fourthParameter)
{

    ...

    SomeOtherMethod(
        firstParameter * 100,
        fourthParameter,
        thirdParameter &&
            secondParameter.Length > fourthParameter.Length,
        22);

    ...
}
```

> **Jeremy Barton:** We don’t have a set line length as part of our style guidelines. I set my IDE to give a guide line at 120 characters, which is generally narrow enough to avoid horizontal scrolling for most IDE configurations and web-based code viewers. However, I treat this as a “soft” limit and violate it when adding the line break makes the line too hard to read.
